title: Evaluating Harnesses: Gates That Hold
objective: After this lesson you will be able to build gold conversation sets with per-component attribution, gate harness changes on no-regression rules, and separate harness regressions from model drift.
why: Harness refactors (new memory policy, rewritten guardrail, loop tuning) shift behavior silently: unit tests pass while support quality drops. Gold conversation evals with per-component attribution catch composition effects; no-regression gates block merges that degrade them. Evaluation is the harness's immune system — without it, every improvement is a gamble.

blocks.text: Gold items assert per-component expectations: memory retrieved the preference (memory), router chose correctly (delegation), guardrail blocked the attack (enforcement), draft met contract (node). Each slot names its owner — failures arrive attributed, fixes land precisely. Happy/edge/attack mix; incidents fossilized with the failing component named.

blocks.caption: Component slots make harness behavior assertable end to end

blocks.text: Harness vs model drift: attribute first

Scores drop for two reasons: **harness changes** (your diffs — gate in CI) or **model drift** (vendor updates shifting behavior under identical harness). Distinguish by pinning: re-run old harness version on failures (drift if it also fails), and version-stamp every eval with harness commit + model version. Undifferentiated drops get mis-fixed (tuning prompts for vendor drift wastes weeks).

blocks.caption: 2×2 attribution: harness axis × model axis, vary one at a time

blocks.text: Harness PRs run gold with per-segment rules: overall improvement required, zero segment regressions, attack/money segments veto-weighted. Failing gates block like test failures — behavior is a merge criterion. Gate history (scores per commit) doubles as the drift baseline: model updates re-run the same gates, separating vendor drift from own regressions.

blocks.title: Attribute the drop
blocks.note: Run it: expect MODEL DRIFT, HARNESS REGRESSION, no-drop — in order. Attribution matrix replaces blame ping-pong between harness and vendor with two decisive runs.

items: Gold with per-component slots across happy/edge/attack; incidents fossilized with owners
2×2 attribution (harness × model axes) separates own regressions from vendor drift
No-regression gates block merges; gate history doubles as drift baseline

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice attribution on all three matrices and map verdicts. (b) Write the missing fourth case (both fail) with its verdict and next step. (c) Design the gate rule for a memory-policy PR (which segments must hold, what improvement is required).
hints: Mappings: drift / regression / no-drop (in order) — one axis varied per comparison.
Both-fail → INTERACTION-or-flaky: stabilize gold (rerun for flake) then bisect interaction (narrow the failing component pair).
Gate: memory-related segments no-regression + overall gain; money/attack segments veto-weighted regardless.
exercise.why: Matrix attribution (vary one axis), interaction handling (stabilize then bisect), and gate design (segment rules + vetoes) are the three eval judgments — each decisive, with blame ping-pong ended structurally.
exercise.code: // Attribution-matrix pattern: 2×2 runs, vary one axis, name the quadrant.

quiz.q: Scores drop after a vendor model update, harness untouched. Attribution + response?
options: Model drift (old harness fails too): pin versions, adjust prompts/guards to new behavior, re-baseline gold deliberately
quiz.explain: 2×2 matrix isolates vendor drift: same harness, new model fails. Respond with adaptation (prompts/guards) + deliberate re-baselining, never silent acceptance.

quiz.q: Harness PR passes units, drops edge gold. Action?
options: Block: no-regression gate fires; attribute per component, fix, re-run — behavior gates merge like tests
quiz.explain: Composition effects escape unit tests by construction. Gold gates with per-component attribution block behavior regressions at merge time.

quiz.q: Flaky gold item fails intermittently. Handling?
options: Stabilize (seeds, frozen responses, tolerance bands) or quarantine with reason — flaky gold erodes gate trust either passing or failing
quiz.explain: Flaky gates train teams to override gates — fatal to the whole system. Stabilize deterministically or quarantine explicitly with a fix date.

summary: Component-slotted gold, 2×2 drift attribution, no-regression merge gates, flake intolerance. Evaluation as immune system with version-stamped baselines.
